text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said integration in western economic and military structures remain Slovakia's foreign policy priorities.
- The Associtaion of Slovak Entrepreneuers has criticised a government proposal to introduce wage regulations.

- Canadian oil and gas company Fracmaster has expressed interest in cooperation with oil and gas storage firm Nafta. Fracmaster said it could build drilling equipment in Slovakia for use in its oil fields in Kazakhstan.
SME - The ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said it had information of connections between some opposition deputies and foreign intelligence services.

- Minister of Agriculrure Peter Baco said the government would help those people who suffered damage in the recent floodings and who had no insurance. The cabinet is to reimburse citizens with by up to one-third of the damage.
- The state fund to support exports (SFPE) has extended some 122 million crowns to pro-export programmes during the first seven months of its operations.

PRACA - Austrian President Thomas Klestil said exclusion of Slovakia from the first wave of NATO enlargement was not a coincidence. Klestil said Austria would not like to have a neighbour that is considering having its security guaranteed by Russia.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The U.S. Trade and Development Agency has granted $600,000 to oil refiner Slovnaft to work out a feasibility study to help prepare the refinery's reconstruction project.
- The state labour agency (NUP) has extended a 102 million crown loan for troubled engineering company Detva which should help preserve 1,270 jobs.
